result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.resource_allocation_index()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute resource allocation index for node pairs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L8946-L9007){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.resource_allocation_index(ebunch=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For each pair of nodes `(u, v)`, computes `Σ(1 / |N(w)|)` for all common neighbors `w`. Similar to Adamic-Adar but uses `1/degree` instead of `1/log(degree)`, penalizing high-degree common neighbors more strongly. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ebunch]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of node pairs to compute predictions for. Each pair can use node IDs (integers) or labels (strings). If `None`, computes for all pairs of nodes that are not already connected. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of `(u, v, index)` tuples where index is the resource allocation score. Results are returned with node IDs. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: O(k) per pair where k is the average degree - penalizes high-degree common neighbors more than Adamic-Adar - inspired by resource allocation dynamics on networks - often outperforms Adamic-Adar on social networks ## Examples {.doc-examples} Compare with Adamic-Adar: ::: {#ad1121e9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) # Star graph: node 1 is hub connected to 2-10 graph.add_node() # Hub node 1 for i in range(2, 11): graph.add_node() graph.add_edge(1, i) pairs = [(2, 3), (2, 5)] aa = graph.adamic_adar_index(pairs) ra = graph.resource_allocation_index(pairs) for (_, _, aa_score), (u, v, ra_score) in zip(aa, ra): # Prints e.g., "2-3: AA=0.434, RA=0.111" f"{u}-{v}: AA={aa_score:.3f}, RA={ra_score:.3f}" ``` :::
